title: An equation quadratic in e to the x, and single-term forms
intro: No calculator. Give exact values and show the work that leads to each answer.

parts.label: A(i)

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \ln 5</annotation></semantics></math>, from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(e^x - 5)(e^x + 2) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: Let <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = e^x</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u - 5)(u + 2) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x = 5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \ln 5</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Let <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = e^x</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u^2 - 3u - 10 = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u - 5)(u + 2) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x = 5</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \ln 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain why the other factor in part A(i) gives no solution.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x = -2</annotation></semantics></math> is impossible because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x > 0</annotation></semantics></math> for every real <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math> is always positive, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x = -2</annotation></semantics></math> has no real solution

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(-2)</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined, because no power of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> is negative

parts.sample: The other factor gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x = -2</annotation></semantics></math>. But <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x > 0</annotation></semantics></math> for every real number <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, so no real <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> makes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math> negative: this root of the quadratic in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> gives no solution.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Rewrite 8x+14x\frac{8^{x + 1}}{4^x} as a single power of 22.
parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8^{x + 1} = 2^{3x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4^x = 2^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the quotient is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{3x + 3 - 2x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2^{x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Rewrite ln⁡(x2−9)−ln⁡(x+3)\ln(x^2 - 9) - \ln(x + 3) as a single natural logarithm with no fraction, for x>3x > 3.

accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln \frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \ln(x - 3)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Quotient property: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln \frac{x^2 - 9}{x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \ln \frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \ln(x - 3)</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C

rubric.point: The equation written as a quadratic in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^x</annotation></semantics></math> and factored: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2^x - 2)(2^x - 4) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>

accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^x = 4</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4^x = (2^x)^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = 2^x</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u^2 - 6u + 8 = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u - 2)(u - 4) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Both values are positive: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^x = 4</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
